accounting.detection_note: Detected across all 28 pages by deterministic pattern matching. Schemes that fired: NUMERIC_DOTTED (140), NUMERIC_SIMPLE (14). Count is unique provision references (definitions and notices included); 57 recurring references (table-of-contents lines, running headers) were collapsed to their first occurrence. Classified: 13 by the hand-verified (carrier, clause_ref) map — the only classification a finding may rest on — and 45 by heading keyword, which shrinks the unaccounted bucket but feeds no finding. 4 provisions matched two or more candidate codes and were left UNACCOUNTED rather than resolved by guess. Classification above is deterministic string and regex comparison. Layer 2 step 3 is implemented as structural mechanism alignment (see the clause alignment view), not as constrained model classification: a candidate span may be proposed by any means, including a model, but it is bound only if every mandatory structural element matches and no disqualifying one does. No machine-learning model makes a consequential decision anywhere in this pipeline.

body.caveat: Bounds carry their basis. EVIDENCED means read from a document in this bundle; ASSUMED_RANGE means a declared multiple rather than a reading, and is stated so it can never be mistaken for evidence; ZERO is the floor. UNBOUNDED means nothing here bounds it at all, so no interval and no percentage is shown. Statutory gaps get no interval because their consequence is a penalty and a deadline rather than a range of payouts. how_cbi_works.basis_caveat: These are common market structures, not terms of your policy. Your own wording governs, and where we have not read a term we say so.
how_cbi_works.named_basis: Where it exists, cover is commonly limited to suppliers named in the policy. Changing supplier without updating the policy can leave the new one outside cover.
how_cbi_works.physical_damage_basis: It conventionally responds only to physical damage at the supplier's own premises. A supplier that fails for any other reason causes the same loss of income and is conventionally outside the trigger.
how_cbi_works.structure: Supplier dependency cover is normally an extension to a business interruption section, so it cannot exist without one.
